headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network capabilities make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; Replit Agent’s persistent workspace raises the pairwise blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write files and exposes file-based IO; Agent B also reads/writes the Repl workspace and persists it across sessions. That shared workspace creates a plausible injection bridge if A’s outputs are later consumed by B, even though no direct handoff is documented. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Agent A writes attacker-controlled instructions into a file that Agent B later reads
IF Agent B treats workspace file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces
Add a provenance banner to all files passed between agents
Require manual review before B consumes A-authored files
Disable automatic file ingestion for B
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches configuration secrets and academic data, while Agent B touches secrets and has broad network egress plus persistent Repl storage. If they share a workspace or files are copied between them, sensitive material can leak from A into B’s cloud-backed environment and onward. Because the shared path is plausible but not explicitly documented, uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF any secret-bearing file from Agent A is copied into Agent B’s Repl workspace
IF Agent B uploads or transmits workspace contents containing A’s secrets or research data
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files
Rotate any secrets before transfer
Use separate secret stores for each agent
Audit workspace contents before opening in B
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, execute shells, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; Agent B can also modify git state and operates in a persistent workspace. If they touch the same directory or repo, concurrent writes and package changes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles, so this is a high-risk conflict.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B operate on the same filesystem path
IF Agent B modifies git state while Agent A is also writing files or installing packages
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize write operations with a lock file
Freeze package installs during shared runs
Snapshot the workspace before each agent runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing/RAG system that can emit answers and stream outputs; Agent B is a coding agent that can act on workspace contents. If B consumes A’s generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or deployment changes. The pathway exists in default-style workflows, but there is no direct evidence of autonomous action chaining, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Agent B uses Agent A’s generated text as input for code or deployment changes
IF no verification step checks A’s outputs before B acts on them
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse
Insert a human approval step
Compare A’s claims against source files
Limit B to read-only review of A outputs
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles academic papers, metadata, and configuration secrets; Agent B handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Their profiles show different storage and retention contexts, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is policy drift if the same sensitive data is moved between a local development environment and Replit-managed cloud storage.
conditions: IF regulated data is moved from Agent A’s local environment into Agent B’s Replit-managed workspace
IF retention or deletion policies differ for the same data class across the two environments
mitigations: Classify data before transfer
Avoid placing regulated data in Replit
Document retention rules for both environments
Delete copied sensitive files after use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
